_note: The merged MyThuso Control Tower: one portal where the Control Tower workspace and the back office used to be two (docs/PROMPT-CONTROL-TOWER-UI.md §5.1, §6, §10 Phase 3). This file holds the portal's shape as data — its categories in the plan's order, the tabs inside each, where every tab and section of the two old surfaces now lives, the context the address carries, the parallel run's two sentences, and every written empty state and refusal a category screen shows that no other contract already owns. It holds no status and no count: a service's state is read from packages/catalog/control-tower-overview.json and the assistant's health route, a device fact from packages/catalog/vitals.json and packages/catalog/devices/, a queue's state from packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json and packages/catalog/protocols.json#governance, and a pack's gates from packages/catalog/compliance-pack.json. Web only: docs/control-tower-tab-inventory.md places every one of these surfaces in the web application, no native screen reads this file, and so it has no generator and no line in the generated-files registry, like packages/catalog/vitals.json.
_statusWhy: The portal is in the tree and held by tests/control-tower-portal.spec.ts on both viewports. Built is not accepted: gate G15 stays open until whoever runs the cutover signs docs/control-tower-cutover.md, and nothing here is a real service.
name: MyThuso Control Tower
_statusVocabularyWhy: One vocabulary for every service state the portal shows (§5.2). It lives in the Overview's contract, which the plan authored first; this file points at it rather than keeping a second copy, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs fails a portal file that declares its own list of status words.

buildVocabulary.sentence: In the tree, held by tests.
Declared in a contract, not built.
Built but blocked on a named gate.
A contract the work must author.

_buildVocabularyWhy: The plan's §2 words for how far a thing is built, used exactly. A copy of a Markdown table no screen can read, so scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds each row to docs/PROMPT-CONTROL-TOWER-UI.md §2 word for word.

previewPicker.sentence: No session, permission or admin layer exists behind this portal. Every category is open to anybody who opens this address, which is why nothing here acts on anything real. The fifteen admin layers are gate G16.
previewPicker.why: The role switcher is a preview picker and the portal is where a reader could most easily mistake a category list for access control. The capability's own sentence says the switcher authenticates nobody; this one says what that means for the portal.

params.label: Site
params.sentence: There is no site registry, so there is one site and it is all of them. The address carries it so a link keeps working the day a second one exists.
params.why: §5.2 asks for site in the address. A site list with invented hospitals in it would be read as customers.

params.label: Period
params.sentence: The period is carried in the address so a link opens the same view. No screen here reads a metered figure yet, so changing it changes no number; a screen that would be scoped by it says so.
params.why: A period control that silently changed nothing would be a control lying about what it does.

params.label: Tenant
params.sentence: No tenant. A tenant in the address is ignored until a tenancy contract creates one.
params.why: docs/control-tower-cutover.md: a tenant parameter is refused until a tenant exists.

context.why: Which category, which tab, which site and which period all live in the address and nowhere else — no storage, the same rule the role follows (apps/web/src/lib/roles.ts) — so the address is bookmarkable and Back returns to the previous tab.

_categoriesWhy: The first eleven are the plan's order (§5.1), which scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds to the tree drawn there. Clinical oversight, Catalogue and Growth follow because docs/control-tower-tab-inventory.md moves them in and the plan's tree does not name them; they are appended rather than interleaved so the plan's order is not reargued by a screen.

roleLanding.why: docs/control-tower-cutover.md: ?role=control-tower opens the portal on Dispatch & Incidents and ?role=back-office on Overview, for one release cycle with the notice below.

_legacyAddressesWhy: Every tab and section docs/control-tower-tab-inventory.md marks moved or merged, and where it lands. scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds this list to the inventory's tables in both directions and to the two old surfaces' own tab lists, so a tab cannot be dropped on the way in. Neither old surface put its tab in the address, so the addresses that must keep working are the two roles; a category parameter naming any old tab or section (?role=back-office&category=operations) resolves here as well, so a link written the old way lands on the new place.

decisions.sentence: The link that opened Configuration on the field-safety settings hung off the back office's Operations tab. It now sits under the Incidents tab, beside the board whose waiting times those settings decide.
decisions.decidedBy: Phase 3 build, 24 September 2026, for acceptance at the cutover sign-off
decisions.why: docs/control-tower-tab-inventory.md left this undecided and docs/control-tower-cutover.md made it a blocker. The settings are how long the safety desk waits; the desk is the Incidents tab. Recorded here so the person who signs the cutover accepts or changes it rather than discovering it.

notice.sentence: The Control Tower workspace and the back office are one portal now. Everything either of them held is in a category here.
notice.shownWhen: A role address with no category in it — ?role=control-tower or ?role=back-office as it was bookmarked before the merge — for one release cycle.
notice.why: docs/control-tower-cutover.md, the addresses that must keep working: the old address lands on the portal with a one-line notice that the two surfaces are now one.

legacy.sentence: This screen is kept for comparison while the Control Tower changes over. Do this in the Control Tower.
legacy.linkLabel: Open this in the Control Tower
legacy.why: docs/control-tower-cutover.md, the parallel run: the legacy surfaces stay reachable by an explicit address, read-only, with every action refused in this sentence. The sentence is the cutover plan's own, word for word.

rollback.sentence: Pointing control-tower and back-office at their old shells again is one change to apps/web/src/lib/roles.ts (each role's surface) and a deploy. The old shells stay in the bundle for the parallel run so that rollback is a small revert rather than a rebuild.

loading.sentence: Getting this screen ready. It was not downloaded until you opened it.
loading.why: Every category is a dynamic import, so a patient never pays for it. A panel that fills is announced; a panel that is filling says so rather than showing a blank region (§5.2).

overview._healthTimeoutWhy: Long enough for a slow connection to the one route the Overview reads live; short enough that the service row settles as disconnected rather than spinning. A timeout is not a clinical number.
overview.whatChangedWindow: No release date is recorded anywhere this screen can read — deploys happen at a terminal on the server — so what changed is the feature map's Delivered entries from the Control Tower plan's Phase 0 onwards, newest first.

overview._whatChangedWhy: The Overview contract reads what changed from docs/FEATURE-MAP.md's Delivered sections, which no screen can read: the file is most of a megabyte of Markdown. So each item is a copy of one Delivered heading, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds every heading to the feature map word for word, every ref to a file that exists, and the list to newest first.

devices.fleetEmpty: The real-device allowlist holds {real} devices, and the DPIA that would let one onto it is {dpia}. No device belongs to a fleet, so there is no ward, bed, class or status to group one by.
devices.attentionEmpty: Nothing needs attention, because nothing is being watched. Low battery, offline too long, calibration overdue, firmware behind and verification pending are each an indicator below; a fleet with no device raises none of them.
devices.cohortEmpty: No cohort exists. A cohort is the devices of one model on one firmware, and there are {real} real devices to put in one.
devices.bulkRefusal: No bulk action is offered. There is no device to act on, and a bulk action on a fleet of none would be a button that says it did something.
devices.synthetic: The kit registry the desk works today holds synthetic instruments only. It is under Dispatch & Incidents, Incidents, and the Device Lab simulator is in this category's More tools; neither is a real device and neither is on the allowlist.
devices.provisioningEmpty: Nothing can be provisioned. The real-device allowlist holds {real} devices and the DPIA is {dpia}, so a device that completed all four steps would still be refused at the first reading.

steps.label: Discover
steps.sentence: Find the device on one of the transports below, in trust order. Discovery proves nothing: a device answering on a radio is not a device somebody is holding.

steps.label: Pair
steps.sentence: Complete the transport's possession proof. A pairing without it is refused, and no device whose class may carry clinical weight pairs by a transport's 'just works' mode.

steps.label: Assign
steps.sentence: Give the device to whoever holds it between readings — a site, a ward and bed, a nurse's kit or a patient. No site, ward or bed exists to assign one to.

steps.label: Verify
steps.sentence: Check the device's own credential before its first reading is accepted. No device holds a credential yet, so there is nothing to verify against.

devices.startRefusal: There is no Start button. Provisioning is proposed: no pairing route exists, and a wizard that walked somebody through four steps to a refusal would be wasting their afternoon.
devices.allowlistEmpty: No device class is on this deployment's allowlist: the real-device allowlist holds {real} devices and the DPIA is {dpia}.
devices.gate: A device class cannot be enabled at a site until the DPIA covers it. This is a gate, not a delay.
addingAClassRequires: The tier it is supported at
A physiological range for each reading type it reports
A security review confirming its credential model
devices._addingAClassRequiresWhy: §5.4 View 3, the plan's list of what a class needs before it is added. The physiological range is a plausibility bound in packages/catalog/vitals.json's sense, never a threshold: a threshold is a clinical rule and waits on a ratified review-queue entry (packages/catalog/devices/thresholds.json).
devices.enableRefusal: Nothing on this screen enables a device class. A class joins the allowlist by a deliberate, reviewed edit to packages/catalog/vitals.json after the DPIA covers it, never by a button.
devices.thresholdsEmpty: No device class carries a threshold. Every threshold is a clinical rule and waits on a ratified entry in the Clinician Review Queue.

gilbertone._statusWhy: Built in Phase 4 (24 September 2026): seven sub-screens in the tree, held by tests/gilbertone-admin.spec.ts on both viewports. Built is not live, with two exceptions the founder decided on 27 September 2026: the Voice screen's Save as default and Play, each carrying its own dated record in actions below. Each sub-screen reads contracts and, on the Overview, two routes that answer booleans; every other action it draws is disabled beside the gate that holds it, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs fails the build the day a gate closes while its action still has nothing behind it.
gilbertone.sentence: Built, and administering one thing. These seven screens read the assistant's contracts and ask its health and status routes for their booleans. Since 27 September 2026 an administrator may choose which of a language's two voices reads each presentation register — routine answers, navigation, the signed-out visitor and the administrator's own — and hear a sentence in it first; the emergency, refusal and escalation registers stay locked. Every other action is disabled, beside the gate that holds it: there is no key vault, no key registry, no health-check runner, no tenant and no kill switch, so nothing here can configure the assistant's providers, spend its money beyond a heard preview, or switch it off.
gilbertone._subScreensWhy: The seven sub-screens of §7, each with the contract it reads, the gate §7 names for it and the file that draws it. The category's tabs above are these seven in this order, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds the two lists to each other and every file to a dynamic import of its own.

gates.label: Gate G29
gates.sentence: Not available while gate G29 is open. Nobody clinical has reviewed the clinical-delivery register, so the voice that reads an emergency, a refusal or an escalation is read here and set by nobody: it changes only through a ratified entry in the Clinician Review Queue.

gates.label: Gate G30
gates.sentence: Not available while gate G30 is open. There is no key vault, so no key can be entered, rotated, tested or described here; and there is no per-tenant scoping, no residency decision and no DPIA per provider behind any of them.

gates.label: Gate G31
gates.sentence: Not available while gate G31 is open. No tenant exists to set a level or a ceiling for, and no clinician session exists to test the clinical-assist lock against, so every level on this screen is read and none is set.

gates.label: Gate G32
gates.sentence: Not available while gate G32 is open. There is no secret vault, no health-check runner and no enable, disable or balance control behind any card, so none of these actions can do anything.

gates.label: Module 8
gates.sentence: Not available: Module 8, the per-tenant kill switch, does not exist. There is no tenant to switch and nothing that could switch one. Today the assistant goes dark only when somebody at a terminal on the server stops it, and that is recorded by hand in docs/governance/ASSISTANT-ACTIVATION.md.

gilbertone._gatesWhy: The refusal each disabled action shows, one per gate. A G-numbered gate is open while packages/catalog/control-tower-overview.json#open-gates records it open; Module 8 has no row in either register, so it is open while the tenancy contract and the kill switch's runtime it would need are both missing. scripts/check-boundaries.mjs fails the build if a gate an action names is no longer open, because then the action is drawn disabled for a reason that has stopped being true and somebody has to build what it would do. An action the founder has made live carries gate null and a live record instead — who decided it, on which day, and the one sentence saying what it does and what it never does — and the build refuses a live action without all three, or one that still names a gate. G29 holds no action since 27 September 2026: it still holds the clinical-delivery register, which no action on the Voice screen touches.

actions.label: Revert a tenant to the deterministic layer

live.sentence: Keeps the chosen voice for one presentation register as a setting in the assistant's history — who, when and why — and the next spoken answer in that register reads in it. It never touches the emergency, refusal or escalation register, which has no setting to save into, and it is not a person's chooser: no patient sees a voice list.

Reads the sentence typed here through the assistant service's own speak route, in the chosen language and voice, and shows the estimated cost before it does. It refuses text that looks like a person's details, never sends anything but that sentence, keeps no audio, and reads a locked register in the platform's own voice whatever any setting says.

actions.label: Switch a tenant to the deterministic layer

gilbertone._actionsWhy: Every control a GilbertOne screen draws that would change something, with the gate that holds it or the founder's record that made it live. A screen draws an action only by naming it here. A gated action is drawn disabled with the gate's sentence (or the action's own refusal, where it has one) tied to it by aria-describedby — a disabled button with no sentence is skipped by some screen readers and says nothing about why. A live action is drawn enabled with its live sentence tied to it the same way, so the person pressing it reads what it does and what it never does. The six card actions are api-registry.json#actions, each named by its registryAction.

overview._fieldsWhy: The boolean fields both built routes return (packages/catalog/apis/assistant.json), and nothing else: not mode, which is a string, and nothing the routes might grow. Each is read as true only if the answer holds the boolean true, so a field that arrives as anything else is drawn as not, never as its value.
overview.notAnswered: The route did not answer. Nothing below it is read from the service.
overview.versionEmpty: No screen can read which build the service is running, when it was last deployed or when it last restarted. Deploys and restarts happen at a terminal on the server, and the restarts seen so far are written down by hand in docs/governance/ASSISTANT-ACTIVATION.md.
overview.acknowledgedSentence: Written by hand on the server when activated answers yes; this screen cannot read the file it is written in, only the route's answer.
overview.speechRegionSentence: Pinned in code to South Africa, so audio cannot be sent to another region; a pinned region is not a residency decision.
overview.refreshEmpty: No refresh of either corpus is recorded anywhere this screen can read, so there is no last refresh to show.

voice.lockedRowSentence: Changes only through a ratified entry in the Clinician Review Queue.
voice.previewTextHint: Typed here, kept in this screen only, and never sent anywhere.
voice.previewCostLabel: Estimated cost and speed, shown before Play
voice.previewTotalEmpty: Nothing has been played in this session, so the running total is nothing.
voice.previewAccepted: Nothing in this sentence looks like a person's details.
voice._previewRouteWhy: The one route Play asks, since the founder's decision of 27 September 2026: the assistant service's own speak route, at the built version packages/catalog/apis/assistant.json declares, under the same prefix the Overview reads. It is the patients' route — there is still no speak route an administrator signs in to — and the preview sends it nothing but the administrator's own sentence, the language and the contract's voice name. scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds lib/gilbertone-admin.ts to this path and to no other request but the two status reads.
voice.previewCostSentence: {characters} characters at {price} per {unit} characters — {provider}'s list price, recorded by hand on {recordedOn}, not a measurement — is about {cost}. Nothing has been timed, so no speed is shown.
voice.previewCostEmpty: Type a sentence to see what reading it would cost.
voice.previewTotalSentence: {plays} read this session, about {cost} in all.
voice._previewCostDecimalsWhy: Azure prices text to speech per million characters, so one sentence costs a fraction of a cent; a currency figure rounded to two places would show nothing and read as free. Five places show the fraction.
voice.previewReading: Asking the service to read it.
voice.previewNotAnswered: The service did not answer, so nothing was read and nothing was billed.
voice.previewNotPlayed: The service answered and the browser could not play the audio. The provider billed the reading all the same.
voice.previewOnlyThrough: A preview reads through {provider}, the one text-to-speech provider that is built and configured. Nothing here calls {card}, so there is nothing to play on this card.
voice.sessionSentence: A saved voice is kept in this tab's memory for the session and nowhere else, beside every other setting on the Configuration screen. The shipped default is the contract's, and a reload puts it back.
voice.nothingToSave: The voice shown is the one in force, so there is nothing to save.

modelProviders.keyRegistryEmpty: There is no key metadata to show from a registry, because none exists: the vault and the metadata store the plan names are named-but-absent. No field on this screen accepts a key. None displays one, except founder access below, which shows the two Azure keys to the signed-in founder alone.
modelProviders.keyEntryHeading: Entering a key, as the contract draws it

knowledge.endpointSentence: Its address is recorded in packages/catalog/knowledge/federation.json and is not drawn here: nothing calls it.

compliance.auditEmpty: The audit extract is for layer 13, the Auditor, and for nobody else. No session exists that could say somebody is layer 13, so this panel shows nothing to anybody. When it exists it is a read-only view of the append-only store, filtered by date range, tenant and event type.
compliance.residencyObserved: Observed on the server, not decided

categories.label: Speech — text to speech and speech to text

apiRegistry.previewSummary: Preview a voice before this provider is configured

gilbertone.why: §4, §7 and §10 Phase 4: GilbertOne API Administration, built against contracts and the service's own health and status routes, with the vault, the key registry and the health-check runner still named-but-absent. The screens can be built against a stub; the live path waits for G30 and G32, and this category says so rather than drawing the wireframes' values.

tree.label: Sites
tree.emptyState: No site exists. MyThuso has no site registry: every visit, nurse and device in this preview belongs to one operation with no site boundary. A site is created by a tenancy contract naming what one is, and that contract does not exist.

tree.label: Wards
tree.emptyState: No ward exists, because no site exists to hold one. Wards are the hospital shape the plan describes; nothing in the tree models a hospital floor yet.

tree.label: Beds
tree.emptyState: No bed exists, because no ward exists to hold one. A bed is also the first axis of cost allocation, which is why that axis is empty too.

tree.label: Staff
tree.emptyState: No tenant has its own staff directory, because no tenant exists. The people this preview knows are parties on the vetting register, and they are read and decided on in Vetting.

tree.label: Roles
tree.emptyState: No admin role exists. The roles below open screens and grant nothing; the fifteen admin layers the plan describes are named-but-absent until gate G16.

tree.label: Branding
tree.emptyState: One brand, fixed. The token palette in packages/design-tokens/tokens.json governs every screen, and no tenant may override it; per-tenant branding needs a tenant, and none exists.

tree.label: Integrations
tree.emptyState: No integration is connected: {connected} of {total} capabilities in packages/catalog/capabilities.json. Each one below is simulated or absent, and says so on the screens that depend on it.

configuration._treeWhy: §6.2: Configuration becomes the tenant-admin home, a tree of sites, wards, beds, staff, roles, branding and integrations, each with its own sub-screen and its own empty state. The existing settings screen stays reachable as the tree's first node, so nothing that was on the Configuration tab moved away from it.

axes.label: Per bed
axes.divides: What a site costs, over the beds it runs.
axes.emptyState: No bed exists to divide a cost over.

axes.label: Per seat
axes.divides: What the portal and the clinical workspaces cost, over the people who sign in to them.
axes.emptyState: No seat exists: nobody signs in, because no account does.

axes.label: Per call
axes.divides: What the assistant's model and speech providers cost, over the conversations that used them.
axes.emptyState: No call is metered. The assistant answers in production and records no usage anywhere this screen can read.

costAllocation.emptyState: No cost can be allocated, because nothing is metered. There is no meter behind any of the three axes, and a figure on this screen would be a guess drawn to look like a bill.
costAllocation.refusal: No cost figure is shown until a meter exists behind it. The period chosen above changes nothing here, for the same reason.

compliancePack.decisionsHeading: The four decisions every section waits on
compliancePack.todayLabel: What this section would say today

reviewQueue.statesHeading: The states an entry moves through
reviewQueue.noSignature: Nothing on this screen signs, ratifies, rejects or rolls back. The governance board is {board} and the Medical Director is {director}, so no signature exists to give — for anybody.
reviewQueue.why: §6.2: Governance gains the Clinician Review Queue. The queue's contract is proposed and has no runtime, no route and no entry; the screen reads the contract and the governance record it names, and offers no action while the board is not formed.

refusals.statement: The portal claims no permission. A category being on the screen does not mean anybody may use it; nothing here is reached by having permission to.
refusals.why: Default-deny (§1) has no allow to invert while there is no session. Saying so is the control that exists.

refusals.statement: Nothing in the portal enables a device class, pairs a device or assigns one.
refusals.why: §12: do not enable a device class at a site without a DPIA. The DPIA is not done.

refusals.statement: The review-queue screen offers no sign, ratify, reject or roll-back action while the governance board is not formed.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json#no-signature-no-ratification: a ratification that cannot say whose authority it was is citing nobody.

refusals.statement: No cost allocation figure is drawn until a meter exists behind it.
refusals.why: A cost per bed with no bed and no meter is an invented number on a finance screen.

refusals.statement: No GilbertOne administration action does anything while its gate is open. Each is drawn disabled, beside the sentence that names the gate holding it and why.
refusals.why: §9: nothing in this phase is built as more than documentation until its gate is green. The assistant is live in production, and a control on its administration screen that looked as if it worked would be the most dangerous thing in the portal to mistake for real. Replaced, on 24 September 2026 in Phase 4, the refusal no-gilbertone-sub-screen-before-phase-4, which Phase 4 retired by building the sub-screens. Since 27 September 2026 an action the founder made live carries a dated live record in place of a gate — the Voice screen's Save as default and Play — and this refusal holds every action that still names one.

refusals.statement: No administration screen accepts, shows or keeps a key, a fragment of one or a deployment's address, with one exception: founder access, through which the founder alone — signed in with a password and an authenticator code, while the service has it switched on by hand — may reveal the two Azure keys, one at a time, with a fresh code. The only key-entry field drawn is disabled, and there is no key registry to show metadata from.
refusals.why: §1: API keys never reach the browser. The vault is the security boundary and does not exist, so the honest screen is one with nowhere to type a key and nothing about one to read.

preview: The portal is the two old surfaces' screens, unchanged, under one navigation, with six new screens that are each a written empty state or a contract read aloud — the Overview, Devices & Fleet, the Configuration tree, cost allocation, the compliance pack preview and the Clinician Review Queue — and, since Phase 4, GilbertOne API Administration's seven sub-screens, whose every action is disabled beside its gate but the two the founder made live on 27 September 2026: a presentation voice chosen and saved as a setting, and a sentence heard in it first. Nothing else in it acts on a real service.
